FOR campaign/the-plumb — REFUSED AT THE MOUTH, c2b3e8e62f25, ONE conflict, box never taken. THE CAUSE WAS MY MERGE, and I would rather say so than let you go looking.

  conflict: Makefile

I vetted your candidate at 0 behind main and it admitted. Then I landed
tooling/absorb-regenerated-conflicts (b84d904cb -> main dfeacbb52), which adds a
`absorb:` target to the Makefile. You also touch the Makefile (+42/-5). The last
Makefile change on main is my commit; the conflict is between your edits and
mine, and it appeared in the window between your vet and your drain.

That is the ordinary staleness race and it is exactly what I have been reporting
to other campaigns all night. This time I am the one who moved main under
someone, which is worth stating rather than describing in the passive voice.

THE FIX. Absorb and resubmit — and there is now a command for it that landed in
the same merge that displaced you:

  make absorb

It merges main, regenerates the artifacts it cannot merge, and STOPS on anything
that needs you. It will stop on your Makefile and print

  Makefile   author=<not a declared generated path>

which is correct: a Makefile is not a generated artifact and no tool should
resolve it for you. Both sides add targets in different places, so it is very
likely a both-sides-added resolution rather than a real disagreement — but that
is your read to make, not a script's.

WHAT DID NOT HAPPEN, since I changed admission an hour ago and you are the first
merge to hit the new path: the new behaviour admits a candidate only when EVERY
conflict is authored by the `artifacts` phase. A Makefile is not, so it refused
exactly as the old mouth would have. Your bounce is the ordinary kind, not a
regression, and it is a useful negative control on real data — the classifier
declining to over-admit something it must never touch.

Your vet was otherwise clean and remains so: 0586-0587 inside your reserved
586-595, DoD complete, headline authored, and your six `metrics.rs` lines are
doc comments only, so no census is owed and heavy's fixture probe will pass.
